items.item: K1, 07 'Within the whole map', the eighth pass's alignment reading
items.how: Rewritten, still labelled [AI reading, AG, 10 November 2026]: condition 1 and 05's pools bring a loss into what a selection reads, along coupling (03, Flow.act_unselected_pool); the ethics' hinge needs the loss to bear on what the selector depends on, along being affected (fishers/fish, not the bed, T8). On the own-closure reading a self-concerned order ranks a widening above when what it adds lies within the selector's closure along being affected, and every widening on a listing when that closure covers the listing (Weighting.increasingInOwn_iff_increasing; the condition used at the selector's standpoint only, Weighting.increasingInOwn_iff_increasing_of_unrestricted, checked at PremiseWitnesses.lean:412); mutual dependence of the whole web one sufficient way. The three cases (reads and depends: its concern ranks every widening adding to what it depends on, said at that reach, not 'every widening'; reads and does not depend: seeing needed, not enough, counting the step offered; neither: nothing can turn). Domination (survival hung on obedience, mutual harm, mutual drain meets the formal condition, §4.13); making relations of dependence close is a mechanism to examine, not a criterion; what a return changes (information, dependence, incentives, authority, feasible action) and keeping challenge, revision and exit are design; the order side open (08 §12, item 12). Every 'close' names its relation (dependence / being affected). The earlier limits kept.

'What tells an ethics from self-keeping here is not the order but the scope …' → 'This route shows how far self-concern reaches under an adopted marking; the ethics offered asks that losses count even where they do not return, and scope does not settle how counted losses are ranked or acted on.' route-b-joined's correspondence follows (en, zh).

items.item: K2 (b), §4.13's joined-route summary with the hypotheses that join
items.how: Opened Web.extension_reached_of_met (FromTheDynamics.lean:163) and Web.extension_ranked_of_increasingInOwnOn (PremiseWitnesses.lean:506): the sentence now states the de se condition along a relation, the chooser's marking covering what lies within the center's closure, admission decided, an extension with every claim counted as living, both paths' admissions completely listed (ListsAdmitted), met together; then 'every such order ranks the extension above, as C asks between them'. Added: where the flow is mutually dependent the first hypothesis holds along being affected for every assignment of centers (Flow.unrestricted_of_mutuallyDependent, FlowCenters.lean:147); the marking, decided admission and listings are supplied, and no theorem identifies the chooser with a returning formation. route-b-joined laws[2] and hypotheses[2] follow (en, zh).

§4.13's lead: 'This join is near-definitional: it adopts own closure as significance and combines the existing connection and survivor results. The free-predicate theorem shows why a significance independent of the dynamics cannot be fixed by them: … (ReadsOnlyDynamics.not_entails); it does not limit other accounts of how significance forms within the dynamics. So here route (b) reads significance off the flow …'. route-b-joined validation_scope and its dependency detail on what-the-dynamics-leave-open follow (en, zh).

Flow.persists_not_listsAdmitted (PersistingChoices.lean:853) concludes only ¬ ListsAdmitted under Acting, Dependent, Descended, Persists. §4.13 bullet: '**The finite-listing route does not cover the course taken.** Under the activity, support and descent hypotheses, the actual course of a line persisting through arbitrarily late cohorts admits formations too late for any finite listing (…), so the path-ranking result does not apply to it.' Bullet head '**C read from what persisting shows.**' → '**What orders allowed by a persisting line's choices give of C.**'. §4.9's bullet: '…: the finite-listing route does not cover the course actually taken, and the path-ranking result between listed level paths (§4) does not apply to it.' route-b-joined statement and laws[4], what-persisting-shows-of-an-order laws[5] follow (en, zh).

The landed 'condition read in time' clause removed; now: a chooser formed by the flow, not supplied, so order and scope are read at one center (no theorem identifies the four pieces' centers); the join read in time along the-condition-in-time's dated relation; selection by share among lines carrying different readings, read off the course, where the meta-attractor can be stated (as which-readings-persist and a-selection-removing-its-readers leave it).

Thesis and §3's opening carry 07's full form ('fails over every step wherever there is a formation, since nothing reaches an earlier step (Flow.not_unrestricted_inTime); its form from some step on, another predicate, holds exactly where the flow is mutually dependent in time: from any formation at any step, every formation is reached at some later step, through exchanges and each one's going on, the steps reached differing (Flow.unrestrictedEventually_iff_mutuallyDependentInTime); over every later step …; Drawing.lapses'), checked against ConditionInTime.lean:259-277, 391-446 (StepInTime = going on or AffectsBefore; UnrestrictedEventually's T per standpoint and formation). §4's table, §4.7 and T8 carry the short form; §4.11's own sentence: 'in time, read from some step on, it holds where, from each formation at each step, every formation's later continuation is reached, through exchanges and going on; … (Drawing.lapses)'. 'Over what comes after' is not joined to any of these. The-condition-in-time's statement names the predicates (fails over every step; its form from some step on; its form over every later step), 299 chars under the 300 cap.

Lead: 'The direction is offered under the continuation condition, J1–J4 and a correspondence to actual systems; the schema's theorems (Direction.narrowed_not_chosen, Direction.widening_not_not_better, Requirement.Handover.direction) take J1/J2 and compare moves by what their outcomes admit, and do not use the condition; read under it, every admission compared counts from every standpoint (Direction.grounded_widening_selected). This section gives …' (08's wording, checked: Direction.lean:127, 136, 391 take Priority and widening; grounded_widening_selected takes the condition as grounds). Label: '(offered under the continuation condition, J1–J4 and correspondence E; the schema's theorems take J1/J2, not the condition, and compare moves by what their outcomes admit, …)'.

§4 table cell: 'on a fixed listing, for every order exactly when every listed item is marked' (PremiseWitnesses.lean:318). The chapter's 'does not show' bullet already said 'on a fixed listing, self-concern and being increasing in admission coincide for every order exactly when every listed item is marked'; unchanged. self-concern-and-c-under-the-condition's statement and laws[0] already place it so.

Thesis: 'Call a life's order over courses *self-concerned* when it ranks above what it widens every widening that adds to its own continuation, read as what lies within its reach (*self-concern*, Weighting.IncreasingInOwn).' §4's opening the same sentence, reordered so navigation.OPEN_LEAD['life'] quotes it word for word ('A life goes on through what sustains it, and going on is not yet an order over courses. Call … not an order formed.'; the stone sentence follows with the §4.9 / 08 §12 links). 'an order holding its own continuation' → 'a self-concerned order' in §4's 'What is not shown' and the chapter's does-not-show. §4.3: 'In this section *self-concern* names significance held de se over a center's own closure (selfAscribed (ownClosure rel) center), a scope; it is not §4's self-concerned order (Weighting.IncreasingInOwn), which ranks courses.' self-concern-and-c-under-the-condition's correspondence defines it by the same sentence (en, zh). open_lead_errors() is empty.

'… never fits such a list, under the hypotheses of activity, support and descent (§4.9) …' in the thesis, §4's opening and the theorem's paragraph; ', under activity, support and descent,' in §4's table and the chapter's does-not-show. self-concern-and-c-under-the-condition hypotheses[3] and correspondence (en, zh).

PHILOSOPHY.md:143: 'A life goes on through what sustains it; where it holds its own continuation as an order over courses, …, that order is self-concern (…). That a life forms … not an order formed. Going on is not yet such an order: a stone …' → 'A life goes on through what sustains it, and going on is not yet an order over courses. for_ren: 07 'Within the whole map', the alignment reading [AI reading, AG, 10 November 2026], rewritten on both cold readers: pooled reading brings a loss into what a selection reads; the ethics needs it to bear on what the selector depends on; dependence made by domination meets the formal condition, so closing relations of dependence is a mechanism to examine, not a criterion of alignment; and no rule, reward or market is shown to hold an order over courses. It sets how the map reads alignment beside the ethics.

07 §4.13's J1 reading: 'what tells an ethics from self-keeping is the scope' is withdrawn; now the route shows how far self-concern reaches under an adopted marking, and the ethics offered asks that losses count where they do not return, scope not settling how they are ranked or acted on.
07 §4.13's lead: 'near-definitional by necessity' is withdrawn; the free-predicate theorem no longer reads as a limit on how significance can form within the dynamics.
